title: 10 best mobile device management (MDM) solutions and tools in 2025
summary: Compare the 11 best mobile device management (MDM) solutions and tools for securing company devices, including Rippling, Jamf, and Iru.
body_markdown:
A growing device fleet creates more work for IT teams than simply tracking who has what. Every new hire, role change, and departure can mean another device to configure, secure, update, or recover. Each update means a new or changed cell in a different spreadsheet. As volume increases, so does the likelihood of manual errors, and these singular misses can add up to become a crisis if not caught and remedied fast.


Mobile device management software replaces disconnected spreadsheets with a single console that enrolls devices, enforces security policies, pushes app and OS updates, and locks or wipes devices that walk off.


This guide compares 11 of the best[MDM](https://www.rippling.com/glossary/mdm) software solutions based on their core device management and security capabilities. It also looks at operating system support, integrations, usability, pricing, and customer-reported limitations.


## The 11 best mobile device management (MDM) solutions to consider


Here's each tool's best fit and lowest published price.


**Best for**


**Features**


**Starting price**

## Methodology


The goal of this list was to build an objective comparison of the best MDM software platforms. Rippling sells MDM software, so every platform was measured against the same six criteria, using the same sources.


For each tool, I reviewed vendor documentation and published pricing, checked product documentation (and demos where available), and read verified reviews across trusted sites (like G2, Capterra, and TrustRadius) to identify recurring complaints.


-


**Features, security, and compliance:** Core tools for enrollment, app deployment, remote support, and device security, along with automation and compliance reporting.


-


**Cross-platform support:** How well each platform supports iOS, Android, Windows, macOS, and other operating systems, including the maturity of non-Apple support.


-


**Integrations:** Connections with identity providers, HR systems, and other IT tools, including whether integrations are native or require third-party connectors.


-


**Pricing:** Whether pricing is per device, per user, or bundled, and how costs scale. Prices are sourced from vendor websites as of September 2026. Where pricing isn’t public, we’ve noted it.


-


**User sentiment:** Each con is based on recurring themes in verified G2 and Capterra reviews.


***Rippling editorial policy:*** *Rippling puts our customers (and prospective customers!) first. The Rippling team is committed to providing information supported by product data, insights, and customer feedback to inform our content.*


## 1. Rippling IT


Most MDM tools start working when a device is handed over. Rippling starts the moment a candidate accepts an offer.


[Rippling IT](https://www.rippling.com/blog/rippling-mdm-review) uses the same employee record as HR and payroll to automate device management. It can order, configure, and ship Windows and Mac laptops before a new hire’s start date, while automatically applying role-based apps, security settings, and device enrollment. The Rippling Agent supports Windows 11 (Pro, Enterprise, and Education editions), the three most recent versions of macOS, and iOS/iPadOS 17.2 and above, with[SentinelOne integration](https://www.rippling.com/blog/rippling-sentinelone-autonomous-endpoint-security) for threat detection and warehouses in the US, Canada, the UK, the EU, and Australia.[Rippling AI](https://www.rippling.com/platform/ai) lets admins ask about a device, threat, or compliance gap in plain language. It answers from live device records, automates the fix or builds an audit-ready report, and inherits each admin's existing permissions. It also runs[offboarding logistics](https://www.rippling.com/blog/how-rippling-runs-it-ensuring-smooth-offboarding) , from generating the return label to routing the device to the nearest warehouse.


Rippling’s[State of the IT Leader](https://www.rippling.com/resources/itleaderreport) report revealed that 72.5% of IT leaders prefer an integrated or unified setup for IT and HR software, and 89.6% favor consolidating their existing tools. Rippling IT, which includes MDM, is built specifically for these purposes, as reflected in its ratings. The platform holds a[4.7/5 average rating on G2](https://www.g2.com/products/rippling-it/reviews) across more than 1,100 reviews.


On TrustRadius, a[technology manager](https://www.trustradius.com/reviews/rippling-2026-07-08-12-40-14) who oversees device management says it means less time guessing who has which device and faster decisions on device upgrade plans, and a[people operations lead](https://www.trustradius.com/reviews/rippling-2026-04-22-07-16-42) reports a 30-40% decrease in onboarding time from automating routine tasks like approving permissions and access.


**Use Rippling if** you want device provisioning running on the same record as identity and HR data.


**Pros**


**Cons**


Less time tracking who has which device


Workflow, policy, and integration setup takes time


Faster onboarding, per one reviewer


Platform documentation could be clearer


### Pricing


Device management starts at $8/employee/month for core capabilities like automated setup, policy enforcement, and remote lock and wipe. Final pricing depends on which modules you bundle.


### Key features


-


**HR-linked provisioning:** New hires' devices are ordered, configured, and shipped automatically based on their role and department.


-


**Cross-platform coverage:** Manages Windows, macOS, iOS, and iPadOS from a single console.


-


**Rippling AI:** Plain-language questions about devices, threats, and compliance, with automated remediations and audit-ready reports.


-


**Inventory and warehousing:** Physical device storage, condition tracking, and reassignment without a separate ITAM tool.


## 2. Iru (formerly Kandji)


Kandji rebranded as Iru in October 2025 and expanded endpoint management from Apple devices to Windows and Android devices. Its automation still runs deepest on Mac, iPhone, iPad, and Apple TV, with Blueprints, 230+ Auto Apps with zero-touch patching, and compliance templates for frameworks like Center for Internet Security (CIS). If your fleet is mostly Mac, iPhone, and iPad, Iru automates much of the Apple management work for you. It’s rated[4.9/5 on Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/181954/Iru/reviews/) from 489 reviews. On TrustRadius, an[IT administrator at a 201–500-person company](https://www.trustradius.com/reviews/kandji-2025-07-24-12-31-55) uses it to automate device provisioning, enforce security policies, and deploy software and patch updates at scale, and an[IT analyst managing close to 100 Macs](https://www.trustradius.com/reviews/kandji-2025-07-23-13-28-07) says it saved their team over 20 hours a week compared with Intune and helped them secure SOC 2 compliance. Weigh the gaps, though: the IT administrator cites limited cross-platform support, restricted customization for advanced workflows, and a higher cost, while the IT analyst flags BYOD controls and containerization as weak spots.


**Use Iru if** you run an Apple-majority fleet and want out-of-the-box compliance frameworks.


**Pros**


**Cons**


Automates provisioning, security policies, and patching


Limited cross-platform support


Saved 20+ hours a week vs. Intune


Weak BYOD controls and containerization


### Pricing


Quote-only. Iru doesn't publish a per-device rate, and its EDR, vulnerability management, identity, and compliance products are each quoted separately.


### Key features


-


**Blueprints:** Pre-built policy templates that apply consistent configurations across device groups.


-


**Auto Apps:** 230+ pre-packaged apps with automated deployment and zero-touch patching.


-


**Compliance templates:** Ready-made baselines for frameworks like CIS.


## 3. JumpCloud


For teams trying to retire[Active Directory](https://www.rippling.com/blog/ldap-vs-active-directory) without replacing it with multiple separate tools, JumpCloud folds the directory itself into the MDM. It manages Windows, macOS, and Linux endpoints and bundles SSO, MFA, LDAP/RADIUS, and OS and third-party patching. Conditional access can gate resources based on device trust. If you want to replace a traditional directory like Active Directory and manage devices from the same console, JumpCloud is built around that. G2 users rate it[4.5/5](https://www.g2.com/products/jumpcloud/reviews) across roughly 4,000 reviews, the largest review base of any tool here. On G2, an[IT business analyst](https://www.g2.com/products/jumpcloud/reviews/jumpcloud-review-13551950) says managing Mac and Windows devices, users, and policies works well, and remote device connections work well. A[reviewer at a mid-market company](https://www.g2.com/products/jumpcloud/reviews/jumpcloud-review-13616775) calls the interface lightweight and fast, says setup and Google Workspace integration were quick, and uses JumpCloud to secure Mac and iOS devices remotely and track lost or stolen hardware. Check platform coverage and admin workflows first, though: the IT business analyst notes there’s no Chromebook support and limited Linux support for apps, and that pulling users out of policy groups for troubleshooting disrupts other syncs, while[another reviewer](https://www.g2.com/products/jumpcloud/reviews/jumpcloud-review-13500871) says recent updates made navigation harder, with too many pop-ups.


**Use JumpCloud if** you’re replacing Active Directory and an MDM at the same time.


**Pros**


**Cons**


Mac and Windows management with easy policy setup


No Chromebook support and limited Linux app support


Fast, lightweight interface with quick setup


Recent updates made navigation harder


### Pricing


The Device Management package costs $9/user/month billed annually ($11 monthly), with single features from $3/user/month.


### Key features


-


**Unified directory + device management:** One console for identity, SSO, and endpoints.


-


**Conditional access:** Policies based on device compliance and context.


-


**Cross-platform patch management:** OS and third-party app patching across Windows, macOS, and Linux.


## 4. Jamf


Jamf built its platform around Apple device management and offers deep enterprise tooling, including zero-touch deployment through Apple Business Manager, Smart Groups, and Self Service. The platform now supports Android through Jamf for Mobile but doesn’t manage Windows devices. Jamf Connect and Jamf Protect extend its capabilities into identity and security.


Teams with a mostly Apple fleet that need more control than a lightweight MDM offers tend to end up on Jamf, and this is how it earns a[4.7/5](https://www.g2.com/products/jamf/reviews) across more than 2,300 G2 reviews. An[information systems administrator at a mid-market company](https://www.g2.com/products/jamf/reviews/jamf-review-9997115) credits Jamf's close work with Apple for keeping it ready to deploy as soon as new OS versions ship. They also found setup fairly easy with the paid onboarding support. A[lead software engineer at an enterprise](https://www.g2.com/products/jamf/reviews/jamf-review-397009) says it handles anywhere from 10 to 10,000 devices comfortably and praises Jamf's in-house support team for fast responses. That depth has a cost. The engineer says the learning curve can overwhelm new admins, parts of the interface feel dated, and pricing can be a stretch for smaller teams. The systems administrator would like Jamf's separate products brought together in one console.


**Use Jamf if** you manage hundreds of Macs, iPhones, and iPads and need the deepest Apple tooling available.


**Pros**


**Cons**


Stays current with new Apple OS releases


Steep learning curve for new admins


Scales from 10 to 10,000 devices, with in-house support


Products are split across separate consoles


### Pricing


Jamf for Mac costs $12.50/device/month and includes Jamf Connect and Protect. Jamf for Mobile costs $5.75/device/month. Both are billed annually with a minimum of 25 devices. Jamf Now starts at $4/device/month for organizations with fewer than 25 employees.


### Key features


-


**Declarative device management (Blueprints):** Devices self-configure based on policy rather than waiting on server push commands.


-


**Self-service:** Employees install approved apps without IT tickets.


-


**Modular security add-ons:** Jamf Protect and Jamf Connect extend MDM into full endpoint security and identity.


## 5. ManageEngine Mobile Device Manager Plus


Mobile Device Manager Plus helps IT teams enroll, manage, and secure devices across iOS, Android, Windows, macOS, and ChromeOS. IT teams can use QR codes, Android zero-touch, Apple Business Manager, or Samsung Knox to streamline enrollment, while kiosk mode lets them lock devices to a single app or a set of approved apps.


Budget-conscious IT teams juggling Android, iOS, and Windows devices will find a lot to like in Mobile Device Manager Plus. G2 users give it[4.5/5](https://www.g2.com/products/manageengine-mobile-device-manager-plus/reviews) across about 250 reviews, and Capterra reviewers rate it[4.6/5](https://www.capterra.com/p/132201/ManageEngine-Mobile-Device-Manager-Plus/) from more than 850. A[senior system engineer at a small business](https://www.g2.com/products/manageengine-mobile-device-manager-plus/reviews/manageengine-mobile-device-manager-plus-review-12810170) manages all three platforms from one console. They say real-time remote troubleshooting and secure app deployment save their IT team a lot of time. A[system admin at another small company](https://www.g2.com/products/manageengine-mobile-device-manager-plus/reviews/manageengine-mobile-device-manager-plus-review-12852705) has found enrollment, policy management, and app distribution reliable from the start, with responsive support when needed. They can also push, update, or remove apps remotely in a few clicks. The most common complaint is the interface: both reviewers call it dated. The system engineer also sees occasional lag when applying policy updates to many devices at once. An[information systems support technician](https://www.g2.com/products/manageengine-mobile-device-manager-plus/reviews/manageengine-mobile-device-manager-plus-review-12549168) found the online setup instructions confusing at first, though support helped them finish the basic setup.


**Use ManagineEngine if** you want a platform that you can pilot without a contract.


**Pros**


**Cons**


Manages Android, iOS, and Windows from one console


Dated, cluttered interface


Reliable enrollment, policies, and app distribution


Setup documentation can be confusing


### Pricing


Free for up to 25 devices. Cloud Standard starts at $645/year for 50 devices and on-premises Standard at $495/year, and each extra technician adds $345/year.


### Key features


-


**Multiple enrollment paths:** QR code, Android zero-touch, Apple Business Manager, Samsung Knox.


-


**Kiosk mode:** Single-app and multi-app lockdown for dedicated-use devices.


-


**ManageEngine suite integration:** Ties into ServiceDesk Plus for ticketing and asset management.


## 6. Scalefusion


Scalefusion helps IT teams manage and secure endpoints across Windows, macOS, Linux, ChromeOS, iOS, and Android. Its OneIdP add-on handles[identity and access management](https://www.rippling.com/glossary/iam) , while the Veltar suite adds content filtering, VPN, and mobile threat defense. Scalefusion tends to appeal to teams that want broad OS coverage without enterprise-level pricing. It holds a[4.7/5 on G2](https://www.g2.com/products/scalefusion/reviews) across roughly 400 reviews, and a[4.8/5 on Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/156745/MobiLock-Pro/reviews/) . Scalefusion also scores highest on the item most MDM vendors lose points for, with Capterra reviewers giving it a 4.9/5 for customer service. A[reviewer at a mid-market IT services company](https://www.g2.com/products/scalefusion/reviews/scalefusion-review-13233755) says the centralized web console is easy enough for less technical teammates to use. It covers both Windows and macOS, and the reviewer says it costs a fraction of what many enterprise competitors charge. On the Android side, a[digital platforms analyst](https://www.g2.com/products/scalefusion/reviews/scalefusion-review-12964984) uses it to push APKs and updates remotely, with a dashboard that shows device status at a glance. A[staff SRE](https://www.g2.com/products/scalefusion/reviews/scalefusion-review-12853527) says enrolling a device takes little more than visiting a URL and entering a code. Reviewers do note a few rough edges. The analyst finds APK deployments occasionally slow or inconsistent, with little error detail when an install fails. The SRE notes that certain compliance features aren't available in every license tier.


**Use Scalefusion if** you prioritize excellent customer service.


**Pros**


**Cons**


Simple web console at a lower price than enterprise tools


APK installs can be slow, with limited error details


Quick enrollment with a URL and code


Some compliance features depend on license tier


### Pricing


The Essential plan starts at $2/device/month billed annually. Windows Autopilot and patching start on Business ($5/device/month), and OneIdP and Veltar start at $4 and $3 per device per month.


### Key features


-


**Kiosk mode:** Single- and multi-app lockdown with customization for dedicated-use devices.


-


**OneIdP:** Bundled identity and access management with conditional access.


-


**Veltar security suite:** Web filtering, VPN, and mobile threat defense layered onto MDM.


## 7. Hexnode


Hexnode helps IT teams manage and secure devices from a single console, with support for iOS, Android, Windows, macOS, tvOS, and Fire OS. IT teams can also use kiosk modes to restrict devices to approved apps or websites and connect Hexnode with tools such as Active Directory, Entra ID, Apple Business Manager, and Samsung Knox. Hexnode is a good fit for IT teams that manage a bit of everything: Windows laptops, MacBooks, iPhones, Android devices, and kiosks. This breadth of support, alongside its intuitive interface, has helped bring Hexnode to a 4.6/5 rating on both[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/hexnode-uem/reviews) and[Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/146405/Hexnode-MDM/) . An[IT specialist at a mid-market company](https://www.g2.com/products/hexnode-uem/reviews/hexnode-uem-review-13134467) likes being able to build one compliance policy for iOS, Android, macOS, Windows, and Linux, instead of recreating profiles for each OS. They also value its native sync with Entra ID, Google Workspace, Okta, and Active Directory. An[IT operations coordinator](https://www.g2.com/products/hexnode-uem/reviews/hexnode-uem-review-12917877) calls the console clean and uncluttered, and says end users don't notice it running. Day-to-day reliability draws the sharpest criticism. A[senior IT systems operations manager](https://www.g2.com/products/hexnode-uem/reviews/hexnode-uem-review-12907967) reports that actions sometimes sat in a queue for up to an hour before reaching devices. They also describe one incident in which apps were removed from hundreds of deployed Android devices and users couldn't reinstall them. A[service manager at a charity](https://www.g2.com/products/hexnode-uem/reviews/hexnode-uem-review-12981023) found that automating updates for common apps required a higher tier, so app updates on their plan are a manual process.


**Use Hexnode if** you’re a small IT team covering a mixed fleet on a tight budget.


**Pros**


**Cons**


One policy workflow across all major operating systems


Actions can sit queued for up to an hour


Clean, intuitive console that stays out of users' way


Automated app updates require a higher tier


### Pricing


Pro starts at $2.20/device/month, billed annually, with a 15-device minimum. Geofencing and directory integration start on Enterprise ($3.20), and Windows Autopilot on Ultimate ($4.70).


### Key features


-


**Cross-OS console:** Manages iOS, Android, Windows, macOS, tvOS, and Fire OS from a single console.


-


**Containerization:** Separates corporate and personal data for BYOD scenarios.


-


**Geofencing (Enterprise plan and up):** Location-based policies that trigger when devices enter or leave defined areas.


## 8. Microsoft Intune


Microsoft Intune is a cloud-based UEM with native ties to Entra ID, Defender, and Microsoft 365. Plan 1 covers cross-platform device management, app management, and endpoint analytics. Plan 2 adds specialty devices such as AR/VR headsets, plus firmware-over-the-air updates.


For organizations already standardized on Microsoft 365, Intune is often the path of least resistance, since it may already be included in their licensing. Intune holds a[4.5/5 rating on Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/230703/Microsoft-Endpoint-Manager-MEM/) across over 40 reviews. Reviewers on G2's listing for Intune's Enterprise Application Management add-on describe what it's like in practice. A[senior network engineer](https://www.g2.com/products/microsoft-intune-enterprise-application-management/reviews/microsoft-intune-enterprise-application-management-review-12753333) says the Android Enterprise integration makes it easy to configure phones and add or remove apps. They also say that managing every aspect of their Windows computers from one console saves a lot of time. A[principal cybersecurity specialist](https://www.g2.com/products/microsoft-intune-enterprise-application-management/reviews/microsoft-intune-enterprise-application-management-review-12216692) highlights Azure AD conditional access, which keeps noncompliant devices away from sensitive apps and data. They also like having endpoint protection policies and firewall rules in one place. Getting full value from Intune takes real expertise. The same specialist describes a steep learning curve, vague error messages that make troubleshooting hard, and support for only a limited set of Linux distributions. The network engineer found Windows enrollment confusing when linking users from an on-premises Active Directory.


**Use Microsoft Intune** if you manage a Windows-first fleet and hold an existing compatible Microsoft subscription (such as Microsoft 365 E3/E5 or EMS E3/E5).


**Pros**


**Cons**


One console for Windows and Android device policies


Steep learning curve and vague error messages


Conditional access keeps noncompliant devices out


Windows enrollment can be confusing with on-premises Active Directory


### Pricing


Plan 1 is included in Microsoft 365 E3, E5, and EMS E3/E5, or $8/user/month standalone. Plan 2 adds $4/user/month, and the full Intune Suite is $10/user/month. Microsoft is also rolling select advanced features into E3 and E5, starting July 2026.


### Key features


-


**Entra ID integration:** Identity-based conditional access tied directly to device compliance.


-


**Endpoint analytics:** Proactive insight into device health and performance issues.


-


**Specialty device support (Plan 2):** Management extends to AR/VR headsets and meeting-room hardware.


## 9. SureMDM


SureMDM by 42Gears runs in the cloud or on-premises and supports an unusually wide range of platforms, including Windows, macOS, Linux, ChromeOS, Android, iOS, Wear OS, VR, and IoT devices. Enrollment options include QR codes, Android zero-touch, and Samsung Knox Mobile Enrollment.


SureMDM stands out on this list for the range of hardware it covers, from standard laptops and phones to Wear OS watches, VR headsets, and IoT devices. It also holds one of the highest ratings here:[4.8/5 on G2](https://www.g2.com/products/suremdm-by-42gears/reviews) across nearly 100 reviews. A[CISO at an enterprise](https://www.g2.com/products/suremdm-by-42gears/reviews/suremdm-by-42gears-review-12710435) manages Windows, Linux, macOS, and Android from a single console and says it simplifies releasing mobile apps. A[senior system administrator](https://www.g2.com/products/suremdm-by-42gears/reviews/suremdm-by-42gears-review-12136975) calls it reliable and easy to use, with strong device control, remote management, and security features. An enterprise[system engineer](https://www.g2.com/products/suremdm-by-42gears/reviews/suremdm-by-42gears-review-12675156) singles out its dynamic jobs and user-friendly console. Reviewers' main asks are around policies and device organization. The senior system administrator says changes often require creating separate profiles, which gets hard to manage at scale; they'd prefer a base profile with override rules. The system engineer misses a dynamic search option for grouping devices on the fly.


**Use SureMDM if** your fleet goes beyond laptops and phones into non-traditional devices like wearables and VR sets.


**Pros**


**Cons**


One console for Windows, Linux, macOS, and Android


Policy changes often require separate profiles


Reliable remote control and security features


No dynamic search for ad hoc device groups


### Pricing


Standard starts at $3.99/device/month, with a discount for annual billing. SureAccess zero-trust network access ($1.99/device/month) and SureIdP ($3.49/user/month) are add-ons on Premium and Enterprise.


### Key features


-


**Flexible hosting:** Choose cloud or on-premises deployment.


-


**Broad platform coverage:** Extends beyond typical MDM scope to Wear OS, VR, and IoT.


-


**Remote support with unattended access:** Troubleshoot devices without waiting for a user response.


## 10. Miradore


LogMeIn Miradore, part of GoTo, is a cloud-based MDM for Android, iOS, macOS, and Windows. Premium adds automation across platforms, and Premium+ adds integrations for user management plus built-in remote support.


Miradore keeps things simple, which is exactly what many small IT teams want. G2 reviewers rate it[4.6/5](https://www.g2.com/products/logmein-miradore/reviews) across nearly 140 reviews, and Capterra users rate it[4.4/5](https://www.capterra.com/p/146147/Miradore-Online/reviews/) across more than 160. An[assistant manager of IT services](https://www.g2.com/products/logmein-miradore/reviews/logmein-miradore-review-13223799) used it to bring nearly 30 company phones under one console for provisioning, security, and decommissioning. They say adding a new device is painless once a profile is set up. An[IT systems engineer](https://www.g2.com/products/logmein-miradore/reviews/logmein-miradore-review-11930343) manages iOS devices with it. They push Wi-Fi settings, passcode and encryption policies, and bulk app installs, and say it works smoothly with Apple Business Manager. A[reviewer at a construction company](https://www.g2.com/products/logmein-miradore/reviews/logmein-miradore-review-13237521) uses its detailed restrictions to lock down company-owned Android tablets in the field without switching to kiosk mode. They rank Miradore's support among the best they've seen in more than 30 years in IT. The friction shows up during rollout and at larger scale. The IT systems engineer finds app deployment laggy, with no automatic retry when an install fails, and says reporting needs a refresh. Another[small-business reviewer](https://www.g2.com/products/logmein-miradore/reviews/logmein-miradore-review-13170882) found that enrollment emails often got lost in employees' inboxes, forcing manual resends.


**Use Miradore if** you’re managing 50 or fewer devices and want a platform that you can execute core MDM tasks on for free.


**Pros**


**Cons**


Painless device enrollment and user assignment


App deployments can lag, with no automatic retry


Detailed restrictions for company-owned Android devices


Enrollment emails can get lost, requiring resends


### Pricing


Free for up to 50 devices. Premium costs $2.75/device/month and Premium+ costs $3.95/device/month, with minimum monthly fees of $50 and $70.


### Key features


-


**Free tier:** Core MDM (lock, wipe, passcode enforcement, inventory) at no cost for up to 50 devices.


-


**Remote support tools (Premium+):** Remote view, file transfer, and session recording.


-


**Directory integrations (Premium+):** Active Directory, Entra ID, and Google Workspace sync.


## 11. SOTI MobiControl


SOTI MobiControl manages large fleets of rugged and dedicated-use devices, such as warehouse scanners, point-of-sale hardware, and field-service tablets. G2 reviewers use it to lock Zebra RF terminals into kiosk mode and to remotely access drivers' tablets.


SOTI MobiControl suits organizations whose fleets look more like warehouse scanners, point-of-sale hardware, and delivery tablets than standard employee laptops. It holds a[4.3/5 rating on G2](https://www.g2.com/products/soti-mobicontrol/reviews) based on 32 reviews. A[software and application engineer](https://www.g2.com/products/soti-mobicontrol/reviews/soti-mobicontrol-review-12385669) values the console's real-time view of every device, which replaced what had been a largely manual compliance process. A[project engineer at an enterprise](https://www.g2.com/products/soti-mobicontrol/reviews/soti-mobicontrol-review-12017655) uses it almost daily to monitor devices and push updates, and calls the support team quick and helpful. ## What is mobile device management (MDM)?


Mobile device management software is a device management system that lets IT enroll, configure, secure, and retire company devices remotely. Apple devices use Apple Business Manager, which also enables supervised mode and its extra controls. Android uses Android Enterprise options such as zero-touch and Knox, while Windows uses Autopilot.


Once devices are enrolled, mobile device management tools can handle:


-


App distribution and license management


-


Inventory management and compliance reporting


-


Separation of corporate and personal data (containerization)


-


[BYOD policies](https://www.rippling.com/blog/byod-policy) and zero-touch deployment


Most MDM solutions on this list now manage laptops and desktops as well as phones, which is why the MDM and UEM labels are increasingly interchangeable. That matters more as[workforces become more distributed](https://www.rippling.com/glossary/remote-work) , and as more company data sits on devices IT never physically touches.


## How to choose the right MDM solution


Use these five checks to narrow the list before booking demos. If procurement needs a formal scorecard, an[MDM solutions RFP template](https://www.rippling.com/blog/mdm-solutions-rfp-template) turns those same criteria into questions that every vendor must answer in writing.


### 1. Make sure it supports your hardware and software infrastructure


Device environment is the least disqualifier on this list, and the last thing you want to do is commit to a platform that doesn’t cover all of your needs. Export your actual inventory from your identity provider or asset tool, then count by device type and operating system.


Match what you have against what each provider offers. Match the tool to the devices you actually run. Iru and Jamf are Apple-first, while Scalefusion, Hexnode, and SureMDM cover nearly every OS. If you need on-premises hosting, SureMDM and ManageEngine offer it.


### 2. Know what you'll pay for the features you need


For each vendor on your shortlist, pick out the plan tier that covers everything you need, as that can drastically change your overall price calculation. For instance, adding Windows Autopilot can more than double the entry price on Scalefusion or Hexnode.


Different pricing models tend to suit different situations better. For instance, per-device pricing suits companies that issue one device per person, but per-user pricing can be better for companies that issue multiple devices per employee.


The other aspect worth considering is the value of consolidation. In essence, can you avoid paying excessive fees for a stack of disconnected tools and instead pay a single bill for a single tool that does it all?

## Frequently Asked Questions about best MDM solutions


What is the most popular MDM software?


Microsoft Intune has the largest footprint because Plan 1 comes with Microsoft 365 E3 and E5 licenses. Among Apple-focused teams, Jamf leads with more than 2,300 G2 reviews.


Can MDM be permanently removed?


Yes, but it depends on who owns the device. On company-owned devices enrolled through Apple Business Manager or Android Enterprise, only IT can unenroll or factory reset the device. On BYOD devices with a work profile, users can remove the profile themselves, which also deletes managed apps and data.


What is the best MDM software option?


It depends on your team. Rippling IT fits companies that want device management, identity, and HR data in one system. Apple-first teams should consider Jamf and Iru, and Microsoft 365 E3 or E5 customers already have Intune Plan 1. Small teams weighing[mobile device management for small businesses](https://www.rippling.com/blog/mobile-device-management-for-small-business) can start free with ManageEngine or Miradore.


Who needs an MDM solution?


Any organization with employees using mobile devices for work can benefit from an MDM solution. This includes companies with remote workers, BYOD policies, compliance requirements (HIPAA, GDPR, PCI DSS), or data security concerns. As workforces become more distributed and mobile devices increasingly access corporate data, MDM has shifted from optional to essential for most businesses.


What features should I look for in an MDM solution?


When evaluating MDM solutions, prioritize:


-


Support for your device types and operating systems


-


Security controls (encryption, remote wipe, conditional access)


-


Zero-touch deployment capabilities


-


Automated policy enforcement


-


App management


-


Integration with your existing IT infrastructure


Also consider compliance reporting, inventory management, remote support tools, and whether the platform offers BYOD support with containerization to separate work and personal data.


What is the difference between MDM and UEM?


MDM (mobile device management) traditionally focused on managing smartphones and tablets. UEM (unified endpoint management) expands this to include all endpoints: mobile devices, laptops, desktops, IoT devices, and wearables. Most modern MDM solutions actually provide UEM capabilities, managing multiple device types from a single platform. The terms are often used interchangeably now, though UEM technically represents a broader, more comprehensive approach.
